en: Mount Mayon in Albay is famous for its nearly perfect symmetrical cone shape.
The Philippine eagle, found in Mindanao, is one of the largest and most powerful eagles in the world.
The Cagayan River is the longest river in the Philippines, flowing through the Cagayan Valley region.
Taal Lake in Batangas is the third largest lake in the Philippines and contains Volcano Island.
Mount Apo in Mindanao is the highest peak in the Philippines, standing at 2,954 meters above sea level.
Palawan is home to the Puerto Princesa Subterranean River National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park in the Sulu Sea is a UNESCO World Heritage site protecting diverse marine life.
The Philippines is the world's top producer of abaca, a plant whose strong fibers are used to make ropes.
The amihan is the cool northeast monsoon that brings dry weather to the Philippines between November and February.
The Chocolate Hills in Bohol consist of over 1,200 symmetrical mounds that turn brown during the dry season.
Benguet province in the Cordillera region is known as the Salad Bowl of the Philippines for its vegetable production.
The Philippine tarsier, found in Bohol, has enormous eyes and is one of the smallest primates in the world.
